source_refs.locator: Executive Summary, printed p. 1 (PDF p. 4), modeled cost of inaction.

evidence.compact_statement: Summary models no-adaptation annual losses at 3-4% GDP by 2030 and 9.4% by 2050; over two million people could fall into poverty by mid-century.

evidence.scenario: Selected adaptation versus no action; assumptions unstated.
evidence.compact_statement: Selected-sector adaptation could add about 2% GDP by 2030 and reduce climate-induced poverty by 45% versus no action.

source_refs.locator: Executive Summary, printed p. 2 (PDF p. 6), coastal exposure.

evidence.compact_statement: Half of Senegal's population and two-thirds of GDP face sea-level exposure; Dakar's population at coastal-flood risk is projected to rise 20-30% by 2050.

source_refs.locator: Section 3.2.2, printed p. 20 (PDF p. 21), historical drought impacts on agriculture and food security.

evidence.compact_statement: The diagnostic reports that the 2002 drought reduced agricultural production by about 35% and the 2011 drought by 20%; estimated production losses across 12 major crops during 1980–2020 totaled FCFA 852 billion, averaging 3.9% of agricultural GDP annually.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

source_refs.locator: Section 3.7, printed p. 28 (PDF p. 29), forward climate-risk analysis.

evidence.scenario: Climate projections for northern drought; cited CCDR GDP range varies by warming assumption and assumes no adaptation.
evidence.compact_statement: The diagnostic says northern Senegal is projected to experience more frequent extreme droughts, particularly in Saint-Louis; its cited CCDR scenarios estimate annual GDP losses of 3.6–4% by 2030 and 7–9.4% by 2050 without adaptation.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

source_refs.locator: Section I, printed p. 3 (PDF p. 3), observed impacts and climate-risk projections.

affected_groups: People whose livelihoods depend on natural resources
evidence.scenario: NDC low-warming scenario for wet extremes; drought-frequency scenario is not further labeled in the cited summary.
evidence.compact_statement: Senegal’s NDC reports declining rainfall, rising mean temperature, sea-level rise, and disruptions to cultivable land, water, and fisheries; it identifies northern regions, especially Saint-Louis, as facing a 20–30% increase in extreme-drought frequency, and identifies more wet extremes in Matam, Tambacounda, and Louga under its low-warming scenario.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

evidence.compact_statement: The study compared Groundnut Basin farmers with Ferlo/Louga agro-pastoralists, linked by seasonal southward herd migration; Ferlo has a long dry season and contested pasture.

pathways.compact_statement: In selected Casamance communities, mines and displacement restrict farming under environmental stress; a conditional reverse-FCV vulnerability mechanism, not climate-caused violence.
alternative_explanations: Poverty, markets, salinization, deforestation and labor constraints can affect food access independently of conflict-climate interaction.
pathways.uncertainty: One purposive cross-sectional study combines respondent perceptions with historical context. It does not estimate a climate-conflict interaction, current mine prevalence or a national effect.
recommendations: Keep the reverse mechanism bounded to the named institution, population and place supported by its cited evidence; do not infer violence from climate vulnerability.
